title: Preferences
description: Communication style, code style, likes and dislikes

sections.title: Code Style
sections.description: Your preferred programming languages, frameworks, and tools

info.overview: Your preferred programming languages, frameworks, and tools. AI uses these to pick idioms and examples that match how you actually work.
tips: Languages: what you reach for by default, not everything you have ever used.
Frameworks: the ones you want code examples written against.
Tools: editors, runtimes and services worth assuming you have.

sections.title: Preferred Languages
sections.$comment: Bare strings with NO usable MCP write path. The generic `preference` entity writes preferences[category][key] = value where value is a SCALAR string (server.py:2199), so it cannot produce an array -- reaching this key through it would overwrite the list with a string. The UI is the only writer. See reference doc 2.4 and follow-up 3.

sections.title: Communication
sections.description: How you prefer AI responses to be formatted

info.overview: How you prefer AI responses to be formatted. This is the baseline; mood overrides below adjust it situationally.
tips: Tone: how it should sound — e.g. friendly but professional.
Detail Level: how much to say and how to structure it.
Locale: spelling and conventions, e.g. British English.

sections.title: Default Communication Style
sections.description: Always active. How you prefer AI responses to be written.

element.description: Update-only singleton for default communication style

fields.name: detail_level
fields.placeholder: e.g. comprehensive with examples, step-by-step breakdowns when explaining code...

sections.$comment: An update-only singleton (identifier: null). All three keys are written literally, not through get_field -- server.py:2211-2219.

sections.title: When I'm feeling...
sections.description: Override the defaults based on your mood or context

fields.name: detail_level
fields.placeholder: e.g. brief and to the point, skip the explanations...

sections.$comment: Stores `mood`. The retired editor wrote this name under `when_feeling`, which no execute_modify branch has ever read -- every MCP lookup resolves on o.get("mood") -- so UI-written overrides were unreachable over MCP and AI-written ones rendered as "Untitled mood". persona_store._normalize backfills when_feeling -> mood with a collision guard. `locale`, which the old editor also wrote here, is NOT stored for an override (server.py:2245-2249) and is deliberately not bound.

sections.title: Response Format
sections.placeholder: e.g. code blocks for anything over three lines

element.description: One statement about how you want answers shaped. Bare strings, like lifestyle's energy_peaks.

sections.$comment: Bare strings. Was five fixed booleans until wave 6 -- a boolean can only answer yes or no to an idea someone else chose, and real preferences are more specific than that. persona_store._normalize converts the old shape, keeping the TRUE keys as text; a list of wants cannot express "explicitly off", and a false boolean already read the same as absent.

sections.title: Learning Style
sections.description: How you learn best, and how you like work approached

info.overview: How you learn best, so explanations arrive in a shape that works for you.
tips: Preferred: the formats that land — worked examples, diagrams, analogies.
Avoid: what reliably loses you — walls of text, unexplained jargon.

sections.title: Likes & Dislikes
sections.description: Things you want every AI to know you like or avoid

info.overview: Standing likes and dislikes every AI should know about, whatever the topic.
tips: Keep each one short and concrete — "unsolicited sales tone" beats "bad writing".
Stance decides which way it reads: like or dislike.
Both stances live in one list, so flipping a row's stance is a single click.

element.description: Something you like; stored in the shared likes_dislikes list with stance=like unless you send stance explicitly

variants.description: Something you dislike; stored in the shared likes_dislikes list with stance=dislike unless you send stance explicitly

sections.$comment: One list shared by the `like` and `dislike` entities, discriminated by `stance`. `stance` used to be in NEITHER entity's required nor optional -- invisible to get_schema though it is the key that decides which entity a row IS -- and was declared here via fields_outside_entity instead. Wave 7 put it on both entities, where it belongs, so that declaration is gone and the node's `stance` binding is now checked against the vocabulary like any other field. See reference doc 2.3 and wave 5 follow-up 4.
